topic: FY2027 OVP budget overview, program delivery, and utilization
summary: The chair limited the briefing to the OVP budget and then recognized the agency to present its FY 2027 proposal. The OVP presented a proposed budget of about 785 million, with over 70% for operating expenses and about 193.1 million for goods and grants under socioeconomic program delivery. It described delivery through 10 satellite offices and one extension office, with a target of about 1.4 million beneficiaries. The agency reported that it served about 1.396 million individuals and groups in 2025, obligated about 851.8 million, and disbursed about 687.8 million. For the first half of 2026, it reported about 773,858 beneficiaries served, 43% obligation of the available allotment, and a 62% disbursement rate, although the spoken disbursement amount was unclear. The presentation ended without a recorded challenge, request, or commitment.
question: What was the OVP's proposed FY 2027 budget, how would it be distributed across personnel, operating expenses, capital outlay, and direct program delivery, and what did the OVP report about program reach and budget utilization? The committee also sought to establish the implementation structure supporting nationwide delivery.
agency_position: The OVP presented the proposed FY 2027 budget as a lean, focused allocation centered on direct socioeconomic assistance, satellite-office operations, and nationwide service delivery. It maintained that its historical utilization, beneficiary reach, project completion, partnerships, and satisfaction ratings demonstrated effective implementation.
outcome: The OVP completed its budget and performance presentation, covering the proposed allocation, delivery structure, beneficiary reach, and utilization record. No member question, document request, commitment, or contested issue was recorded in this stretch.

positions.position: The briefing should remain confined to the OVP budget and should avoid matters already forwarded to the Senate.

thread.speaker: Rep. Alvarez, committee chair
thread.said: The chair said the briefing would be confined to the OVP budget, which had already been reduced compared with 2026. He directed members to avoid issues forwarded to the Senate and set five-minute questioning periods.

thread.speaker: Rep. Alvarez, committee chair
thread.said: The chair observed that the OVP budget differed substantially from the previous year and recognized Attorney Celica Lopez to present the agency's proposal.

thread.speaker: Celica Lopez, OVP undersecretary and chief of staff
thread.said: Lopez introduced the OVP's FY 2027 proposed budget presentation and requested that the committee view an audiovisual presentation before the Chief of Budget Division presented the budget highlights.

thread.speaker: OVP audiovisual presentation
thread.said: The presentation said the OVP served as a direct bridge to underserved and marginalized communities, working with line agencies to expand social protection and deliver relief during emergencies.

thread.speaker: OVP audiovisual presentation
thread.said: The presentation reported that the OVP served 1,390,000 Filipinos in 2025, exceeding its target by 33%, and described its prior satisfaction rating as averaging over 90%.

thread.speaker: OVP audiovisual presentation
thread.said: The presentation stated that the FY 2027 proposed budget was 785,204,000 peso and would support nine initiatives targeting 1,400,000 beneficiaries nationwide.

thread.speaker: OVP audiovisual presentation
thread.said: The presentation described the initiatives as including microenterprise grants, school supplies and other assistance under Padba Bago, You Can DVP, disaster operations, the RISE program, Kalusugan food trucks, Libri Sakay, mobility assistance, and Al Janaza burial kits.

thread.speaker: OVP audiovisual presentation
thread.said: The OVP said it operated through 10 satellite offices nationwide and used them for community engagements, local needs assessment, coordination with local government units, and delivery of assistance.

thread.speaker: OVP audiovisual presentation
thread.said: The presentation reiterated a total FY 2027 budget of 785,204,000 pesos, said over 70% was allocated to operating expenses, and identified 193,000,000 and 103,000 pesos for direct program activities.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: Tenido said the DBM-recommended agency-specific budget was 7.85.2 of 4,000,000, compared with the OVP proposal of 7.07 9,901,000. He said the recommendation was net of ARLIP and 11.7% lower than the FY 2026 appropriated budget.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: Tenido reported a recommended personnel services budget of 235,776,000, or 29.4% of the total, which was 9.7% higher than the FY 2026 personnel services level.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: He said personnel services covered 183 field positions and nine 69 non permanent positions, with the transcript also stating a total proposed PS budget including ARLEAP of 2.03 5,776,000. The figures in the latter statement were unclear.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: Tenido reported a maintenance and other operating expenses budget of 561,651,000, or 70.1% of the total, covering supplies, financial assistance and subsidies, travel, representation, professional services, leases, information-technology consultancy, and central and satellite office operations.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: The capital outlay budget was described as 0.41% of the total recommended budget, equivalent to 3,300,000, primarily for information and communications technology equipment under the OVP ISSP.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: Tenido stated that the agency-specific budget was 785,200,000, with 15,554,000 under automatic appropriations for ARLEAP. He said 193,103,000, or 24.6%, was allotted for goods and grants under socioeconomic program delivery, excluding logistics and other operating costs.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: Tenido said the OVP's budget had generally ranged from 700,000,000 to 900,000,000 before FY 2023, exceeded 1,000,000,000 in FY 2023 and FY 2024 because of medical and burial assistance, and returned to its pre-2023 level with 744,150,000 in 2025.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: He said the proposed 2027 budget maintained the same level as 2025 with cost adjustments, including mandated salary increases, and that the OVP had maintained a full-year budget utilization or obligation rate of at least 85.55%.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: Tenido attributed the decrease in the proposed 2027 budget to adoption of the 2025 budget level and cost adjustments, and said the OVP had consistently used its budget to sustain key programs.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: He listed programs implemented since 2022, including the learners campaign, disaster response operations, relief for indigents and people in crisis, You Can Be VP, Libri Sakay, Kalusugan Foodtrap, Magnigosho Tadai, and medical and burial assistance.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: Tenido said the programs were implemented through the central office, 10 satellite offices, and one extension office covering areas in Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao, including an extension office in Tondo, Manila.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: For FY 2025, the OVP reported a target of 1,047,935 beneficiaries and service to 1,395,867 individuals and groups. It also reported 417 strategic partnerships, implementation of 100% of planned projects, a 98% average satisfaction rating, and 2,906 engagements.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: For 2025, Tenido reported a 93% budget utilization rate, with 851,836,000 obligated and 687,848,000 disbursed, representing an 81% disbursement rate.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: As of June 30, 2026, the OVP reported a target of one million five hundred eleven one hundred sixty eight beneficiaries and service to 773,858 individuals, or 51% of the target, during the first semester. It also reported 85 partnerships, implementation of 100% of planned projects, a 97.96% average satisfaction rating, and 2,724 engagements.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: As of 06/30/2026, the OVP reported a total release allotment of 961,110,000, with 43% obligated, equivalent to 413,970,000, and a disbursement rate of 62% or two five six point three one eight million. The last amount was unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Kelvin Jerome Tenido, OVP chief budget division
thread.said: Tenido concluded that the proposed agency-specific budget was 7.08 5,204,000 for FY 2027 and said it would allow the OVP to continue providing efficient, accessible, and responsive public service. The amount was garbled in the transcript.

topic: OVP enterprise and civil-society grants and post-grant outcomes
summary: Sarah Elago asked the OVP to identify measurable outcomes from its enterprise and civil-society grants, including how many beneficiaries had grown or sustained their enterprises. OVP director Norman Baloro said CSO grants were around 150,000 pesos, individual grants were PHP 15,000 each, and groups generally had 20 to 25 members or clients. He said the OVP conducted post-grant monitoring after ninety days and described monthly meetings, mentoring, and other support activities. Elago pressed for 2023 outcome numbers and an activities report. Baloro committed to provide lists of individual and group beneficiaries, while the requested evidence of enterprise sustainability remained outstanding.

It said post-grant monitoring occurred after ninety days and that monthly meetings, mentoring, and other activities supported sustainability, but it did not present outcome counts during the exchange.
outcome: The OVP described its grant eligibility and monitoring practices and committed to submit beneficiary information. The requested measurable outcome data on enterprise growth or sustainability, including the 2023 figures, was not provided in the excerpt.

topic: Libreng Sakay routes, contracting, and passenger capacity
summary: A committee member asked how the 22,000,000 Libreng Sakay allocation related to the reported 1,400,000 beneficiaries, of whom 1,200,000 were attributed to the program. The OVP said the service operated nine buses nationwide, with routes planned in partnership with the LTFRB, MMDA, and another agency rendered as "OTR," and with private operators including Jackliner, Rural Transit Mindanao Incorporated, Oyinco City Tours, and Kudos Trucking Corporation. The agency said two buses had been purchased by the OVP and that each bus had capacity for around 46 passengers. It described peak-hour operations from 5AM to 9AM and 5PM to 9PM, but the passenger examples of 442 and 422 were unclear and did not fully establish the reported reach. The OVP also projected reaching 4,000,000 passengers around mid-November. The committee requested a list of providers, leaving the capacity and allocation calculations partly unresolved.
question: The committee sought to establish how the OVP's Libreng Sakay allocation translated into routes, contracted operators, bus ownership, operating costs, and passenger reach. It also asked how the reported beneficiary figures were calculated and what capacity the program could actually deliver.
agency_position: The OVP said Libreng Sakay operated nine buses nationwide through partnerships with transport agencies and private bus operators, while two buses had been purchased by the OVP. It said routes were planned by partner transport agencies, operations ran during peak hours, each bus held around 46 passengers, and the program expected to reach 4,000,000 passengers around mid-November.
outcome: The OVP explained the nine-bus operating model, named private transport partners, described peak-hour capacity, and stated that it expected to reach 4,000,000 passengers. The committee requested a provider list, while the discrepancies between the 1,200,000 beneficiary figure, the 22,000,000 allocation, and the unclear 442/422 capacity figures were not fully resolved.

summary: Rep. Renee Ko asked how the OVP selected beneficiaries for bags, wheelchairs, and Aljanaza kits and how it avoided duplication with LGUs and other agencies. OVP Director for Operations Norman Baloro said the Department of Education and people's organizations identified recipients, with priority for GIDA and last-mile schools, while wheelchairs could be provided upon requests from organizations, LGUs, or walk-in clients. He cited dashboard monitoring and a Department of Education-verified master list as safeguards against duplication. The discussion also covered the proposed OVP charter, House Bill Number 4 2 1 5, which the OVP said would establish a dedicated policy-research function; current policy work was handled by the Strategic Management Office. Rep. Ko asked for the OVP or Vice President's position on “Paxilica,” but the agency official declined to comment, said the question would be noted, and the Chair requested any response in writing.
question: The committee sought to establish how the OVP selected beneficiaries for bags, wheelchairs, and Aljanaza kits, and how it prevented duplication with assistance from LGUs, people's organizations, and other agencies. Rep. Renee Ko also asked who handled OVP policy research and whether the office had a policy position on the issue referred to in the transcript as “Paxilica.”
agency_position: The OVP said beneficiary selection relied on Department of Education identification, people's-organization requests, priority targeting of GIDA and last-mile schools, and requests from organizations, LGUs, and walk-in clients. It said dashboard monitoring, a Department of Education-verified master list, and supporting documents were used to control duplication. The OVP said policy research was currently handled by the Strategic Management Office, while a proposed OVP charter would establish a dedicated policy-research office.
outcome: The committee received the OVP's explanation of beneficiary identification and duplication controls, but the extent of coordination with agencies beyond the Department of Education was not fully detailed. The question on the Vice President's position on “Paxilica” remained unanswered and was to be addressed, if at all, in a written response.

positions.position: She pressed for clearer beneficiary-selection and duplication safeguards and sought an institutional policy-research function capable of advising on contentious policy matters.

They maintained that beneficiary identification and verification were conducted collaboratively with the Department of Education and other request-generating entities, while current policy work was handled by the Strategic Management Office pending possible creation of an OVP charter.

topic: Funding and targeting of wheelchair and Aljanaza kits
summary: Rep. Renee Ko asked how the OVP selected beneficiaries for wheelchair and Aljanaza kits and how it controlled duplication with other assistance providers. She referenced one fifty thousand learners and 600 clients associated with the programs. The OVP said wheelchair assistance could be requested by organizations, local government units, or walk-in clients, while Aljanaza kits were made available through the OVP's assistance network and were intended to be provided within twenty four hours after a Muslim death. The OVP said the Department of Education and people's organizations identified school recipients, with priority given to GIDA areas and last-mile schools. It also cited a dashboard and a Department of Education-verified master list as duplication-monitoring measures. The hearing received the explanation, but did not establish a detailed cross-agency duplication-control process.
question: The committee sought to establish how the OVP selected beneficiaries for wheelchair and Aljanaza kits, whether distributions were walk-in or partnership-based, and how the OVP prevented duplication with other agencies, local government units, and people's organizations.
agency_position: The OVP said wheelchair assistance was provided upon request, including requests from organizations, local government units, and walk-in clients, while Aljanaza kits were distributed through the OVP's assistance network in coordination with relevant communities. For school-related targeting, the OVP relied on the Department of Education and people's organizations to identify recipients and used a Department of Education-verified master list and dashboard to monitor beneficiaries.
outcome: The OVP provided a general description of its targeting and monitoring procedures, including Department of Education coordination and verification of school beneficiary lists. The record did not establish a specific cross-agency duplication database or provide a detailed wheelchair and Aljanaza kit process flow.

positions.position: She sought clear beneficiary-selection and process rules and pressed the OVP to demonstrate that wheelchair and Aljanaza kit distributions were not duplicated with assistance from other government agencies, local government units, or people's organizations.

topic: OVP maintenance and other operating expenses and program manuals
summary: A committee member questioned whether OVP programs had publicly accessible manuals and requirements because the OVP directly implemented its programs. The OVP said all nine core programs had regularly updated manuals, although the You Can Be VP procedure was not in the citizens charter. OVP officials explained that the You Can Be VP allocation included program activities and reported five recipients against a target of two learners. The member also questioned Libreng Sakay's cited beneficiary totals and 22,000,000 budget; the OVP described nine buses, private and government partnerships, two buses being purchased, and POL costs charged to the OVP. The OVP cited 46 passengers per bus and a daily figure recorded inconsistently as 442 and 422, with operations during morning and afternoon peak hours. The exchange ended with a request for a list of providers and related You Can Be VP information, while the beneficiary calculations remained unclear.
question: The committee sought to establish whether the OVP's discretionary programs had publicly accessible operating guidelines and whether the proposed amounts and beneficiary targets for programs such as You Can Be VP and Libreng Sakay were justified. agency_position: The OVP said all nine core programs were covered by regularly updated manuals, with some procedures in the citizens charter, although the You Can Be VP program was not included there. It defended the program allocations as supporting activities beyond direct grants and explained that Libreng Sakay used nine buses through public and private partnerships, with the OVP bearing POL costs and purchasing two buses.
outcome: The OVP explained its manuals, You Can Be VP allocation, and Libreng Sakay operating model, but the committee requested a provider list and related program information. The conflicting 442 and 422 passenger figures and the relationship among the cited beneficiary totals were not resolved in the exchange.

positions.position: The member pressed for publicly accessible manuals, clarification of the You Can Be VP grant and beneficiary targets, and an accounting of Libreng Sakay's beneficiaries, providers, and operating costs.

thread.said: The official said manuals of operation covered the programs and offered to have the director for operations explain the detailed process flow for the Pagbabago a million learners campaign, Aljanaza kits, and wheelchair distribution.

thread.speaker: Norman Baloro, OVP director for operations
thread.said: For learners, the Department of Education and people's organizations identified recipient schools, while the special projects division handled assessment and evaluation, project design, and implementation with satellite offices.

thread.speaker: Norman Baloro, OVP director for operations
thread.said: He said the OVP prioritized GDA areas and DepEd-identified last-mile schools, including schools where teachers could testify that it was their first time receiving such government assistance.

thread.speaker: Norman Baloro, OVP director for operations
thread.said: He said the Aljanaza kit was intended to show respect for the Muslim community and could be provided within twenty four hours after a death. The kits were available through the OVP's main and 10 satellite offices.

thread.speaker: Norman Baloro, OVP director for operations
thread.said: He said wheelchair assistance was provided upon request from organizations, local government units, or walk-in clients, including requests for other mobility devices.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She asked whether wheelchair and Aljanaza-kit assistance was provided to walk-in clients.

thread.speaker: Norman Baloro, OVP director for operations
thread.said: He said the learner-selection process began through collaboration with DepEd, including meetings with its regional offices and coordination with the DepEd central office.

thread.speaker: Norman Baloro, OVP director for operations
thread.said: He said DepEd identified priority schools, while people's organizations could directly write the Vice President requesting support. The process included both DepEd schools and Madrasa schools.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She asked how the OVP ensured that its beneficiaries were not duplicated with assistance from the LGA, people's organizations, or other agencies.

thread.speaker: Norman Baloro, OVP director for operations
thread.said: He said the OVP maintained dashboard monitoring and a master list for learners identified through DepEd, with the records and supporting documents verified and signed by DepEd.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She asked whether the master list was coordinated with other agencies so that the committee could have visibility over duplication controls.

thread.speaker: Norman Baloro, OVP director for operations
thread.said: He described the process as collaborative with DepEd and reiterated that the OVP focused on GDA areas and DepEd-identified last-mile schools.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She asked about the OVP's policy direction and whether, as the second-highest office of the land, it had a policy or research arm that advised agencies and communicated policy positions to the public.

thread.speaker: An OVP official
thread.said: The official identified creation of an OVP charter as an institutional project and cited House Bill number 4 2 1 5, which would define the OVP's powers and functions and appropriate funds.

thread.speaker: An OVP official
thread.said: The official said the proposed legislation was intended to empower future vice presidents and institutionalize programs so that the office would not be dependent on the vice president in office.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She characterized the issue as the institutionalization of the OVP and its policy role.

thread.speaker: An OVP official
thread.said: The official said the proposed charter contained a provision for a specific policy-research office. Until then, policy work was handled by Director Shine Farada's Strategic Management Office, in coordination with national government agencies and the private sector.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She sought clarification on the current point person for policy matters and the OVP's expected role in contentious public-policy and budget issues.

thread.speaker: An OVP official
thread.said: The official said legislators sometimes asked the OVP for comments on proposed legislation, and that the Strategic Management Office handled those requests, including correspondence concerning Paxilica.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She asked for the current position of the OVP or Vice President Sara Duterte on Paxilica.

thread.speaker: An OVP official
thread.said: The official declined to comment on the Vice President's position, saying, "I cannot comment on that" because the officials present were authorized only to answer for the office.

thread.speaker: An OVP official
thread.said: The official said the question would be noted.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She said the committee hoped the response would be transmitted to her representation.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The Chair directed that any reply from the OVP team be sent in writing to the committee.
